transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-11
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Sofia Ramirez (Bridgewater - Head of ML Platform), Liam O'Connor (Bridgewater - VP Eng), Priya Desai (Bridgewater - Security Lead)

Summary:
Quick renewal and expansion checkin. Bridgewater wants to add capacity for Q3 peak, enable EU region, and discuss a 12->24 month contract extension for price protection. Security team had follow-ups re: audit logs and KMS. SE will run EU perf benchmarks and AE to send amendment + pricing.

Topics:
- Dedicated capacity sizing and pricing
- Adding EU region and data residency
- Contract extension (term & pricing protection)
- Security: SOC2, audit logs, KMS, VPC/private deploys
- Pilot/benchmark plan

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep this tight, got a few agenda items around your renewal and the capacity bump for Q3.
[00:06] Sofia Ramirez: Yeah thanks Maya, appreciate it. We're coming up on the anniversary and, um, a lot of traffic forecast for September so want to lock in dedicated pools and add the EU region.
[00:16] Liam O'Connor: Quick note on timeline — finance wants to know by end of March if we extend to 24 months to get the price guarantee.
[00:22] Maya Patel: Got it. From Redwood side we can draft a contract amendment to add +2 reserved clusters and extend term. We'll include pricing tiers for the extra capacity and region egress.
[00:32] Daniel Kim: Technical question — are you planning to run inference for high-throughput batch jobs or mostly near-real-time API calls? That affects batching and hardware profile.
[00:40] Sofia Ramirez: Mostly near-real-time for routing + document parsing, but there will be nightly bulk embedding jobs for search reindex. Latency matters for the live calls.
[00:49] Daniel Kim: OK so we'd recommend a mixed pool: reserved Dedicated nodes optimized for low p99 latency and separate batch nodes you can scale down. For p99 under 150ms we usually put customer workloads on 8xA100s with optimized kernels, but we can run bench to confirm.
[01:03] Liam O'Connor: Can you also speak to whether Redwood Dedicated can live in our VPC in eu-west-1? Data residency is a must.
[01:10] Maya Patel: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer VPC deployments and Private control plane options. For hosted/dedicated we also have region pinning in eu-west-1; we can keep the KV cache and logs in EU.
[01:21] Priya Desai: On security — we need SOC2 Type II docs, audit log retention, and how KMS/HSM integration works. Also, are request payloads ever routed outside the region for fallback? We need assurance on data residency and fallback policies.
[01:35] Daniel Kim: Short answer: SOC2 + ISO are available, we have per-request routing policies that can be configured to never fallback to other regions. There's also a Private option with customer-managed networking if you need air-gapped. We'll send the pack.
[01:48] Sofia Ramirez: When you say "send the pack" can you include the performance spreadsheet from last week's PoC? The one with tokens/sec and p99 numbers per model?
[01:56] Daniel Kim: Yes I'll upload the benchmark-spreadsheet and a short runbook. Note that some of the transcribed names in the doc might show Redwood Dedicate or, uh, Redwood Dedi — ignore the typos, it's the same service.
[02:08] Liam O'Connor: Pricing — we ran internal calc and the delta for Dedicated is large, can we get a 10% discount if we commit to 24 months and +2 clusters?
[02:17] Maya Patel: We can propose a stepped discount: 7% for term extension alone, and additional volume discount if committed capacity is above a threshold. I'll include a few pricing scenarios for you to review.
[02:27] Priya Desai: Also need to confirm log retention window and if logs can be forwarded to our SIEM.
[02:31] Daniel Kim: Yes logs can be exported to S3 or to your SIEM via syslog/forwarder; retention configurable. We'll include documentation.
[02:39] Sofia Ramirez: For the EU run, what's the typical throughput difference vs us-west? We had some degradation in last PoC that surprised us.
[02:46] Daniel Kim: Region differences usually come down to available hardware and kernel builds. We'll run an EU bench with 4xA100 and 8xA100 configs and measure p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec. Expect small variance but we'll quantify.
[02:58] Liam O'Connor: On fallback — if eu-west faces capacity constraints, will requests route to us-west automatically? We need to avoid cross-border routing.
[03:06] Maya Patel: We can set routing policy to strict region-only; automatic fallback is opt-in. We'll document the policy.
[03:12] Priya Desai: For KMS — do you support customer-managed keys (bring your own key)?
[03:16] Daniel Kim: Yes, we support BYOK via standard KMS integrations (AWS KMS, customer HSM). We keep data encrypted at rest and in transit.
[03:23] Sofia Ramirez: Great. For the pilot, we want Redwood to run a simulated traffic pattern and then show cost per 1M tokens at the new config.
[03:30] Maya Patel: Perfect. We'll run the pilot and include cost calc and perf numbers. We'll also include Redwood Optimize suggestions — like batching, cache TTLs, and quantization options to reduce unit cost.
[03:42] Liam O'Connor: Any blockers from legal side? We have a couple questions about indemnity clauses.
[03:45] Maya Patel: Legal will include a standard amendment; if you send the exact redlines we'll route them to our GC. For indemnity, we usually follow market standard terms, can escalate if needed.
[03:54] Priya Desai: One more, can we get an SLA for p99 latency?
[03:57] Daniel Kim: SLA for latency is tricky; we provide uptime SLAs and latency targets for Dedicated & Reserved pools. We can surface p99 targets per config and bake them into the SLOs for Dedicated commitments.
[04:08] Sofia Ramirez: OK that sounds reasonable. Recap — you will send: pricing scenarios and contract amendment, SOC2/ISO & KMS docs, EU bench results, benchmark spreadsheet, and a pilot schedule.
[04:16] Maya Patel: Correct. I'll send the amendment and pricing options by next Thursday, Daniel will share the security pack by Friday, and we'll run the EU bench next week.
[04:25] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good. Any open questions from Redwood?
[04:28] Daniel Kim: Just one detail — for the batch embeddings, what size of batch and latency tolerance? That affects how we configure the batch nodes.
[04:34] Sofia Ramirez: Nightly jobs can tolerate up to 10s per request, batch size around 2048 tokens aggregated across 500 docs.
[04:41] Daniel Kim: Great, that'll guide the bench.
[04:44] Maya Patel: Alright thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[04:48] Priya Desai: Thanks all.

Action Items (auto):
- Maya: contract amendment + pricing (due 2026-03-18)
- Daniel: security docs + run EU benchmark (due 2026-03-20)
- Priya: send compliance Qs (due 2026-03-14)

References/Links Mentioned:
- benchmark-spreadsheet (uploaded to shared drive)
- security-pack.pdf (to be shared)
